subject: ARLO SEO — Weekly Pulse — 2026-09-24
html:
Weekly Pulse — Sept 24, 2026

~12 weeks since kickoff (2026-07-04). No code shipped this session — and that's the right call, not a skipped task. Full detail below.

Ranking movement

Fresh live pull (site_id 12704162, 2026-09-17→2026-09-24, daily): average position flat at 100 (not-ranked floor) every day. All 22 tracked keywords remain unranked, unchanged since tracking began.

Backlinks

Flat at 3 backlinks / 2 referring domains, unchanged since 2026-09-10 (2 weeks).

Anything broken?

No. Last 5 SEO Report Email runs (09-11 through 09-21) all green, 40/40 all-time. AI Result Tracker still has zero LLM engines configured — no AI-visibility baseline yet, unchanged, still needs a human to set up in SE Ranking.

Why nothing shipped

The MCP-integration keyword cluster (FOCUS) came back exhausted for an 8th straight session — every term is already targeted by a live page or blocked on a catalog.ts connector that's still "coming soon" (all 8 unchanged, some 4+ months overdue). The destinations-comparison-section path stays closed (Excel/Snowflake/Redshift/Databricks all still gated). Turned to the blog next: the strategy doc's audit says the blog is empty and names "What is MCP" as the first post to write. Drafted it — then, before committing, found the blog actually already has 10 real posts (shipped in earlier sessions, 2026-07-04 through 2026-08-20) that the audit doc's "empty blog" note never got updated to reflect. One of those 10, "What Is an MCP Connector?", covers nearly identical ground to the draft. Rather than publish a near-duplicate, the draft was deleted and nothing was staged. That's a real finding worth flagging: the strategy doc's blog section is stale and should be corrected so a future session (human or automated) doesn't repeat the same near-miss.

Two things double-checked and ruled out

llms.txt's pricing line ($0 → $19 → $99 → $249 → $499) was checked against the actual plan-limits code — it matches exactly, not a bug, just the underlying tier structure sitting under the current "free during early access" promo. And the homepage's old "Trusted by 40+ companies" trust-bar component was re-confirmed to be dead code that isn't rendered anywhere live, so it's not something a visitor or Google actually sees.

Next

With FOCUS, destinations, and now the blog all genuinely caught up against the static audits, the next content session should re-read the technical/on-page/SXO audits end-to-end looking for a new, previously-unflagged defect — the same pattern that's found real fixes the last three sessions running — rather than force new content into an exhausted backlog. Off-page outreach (0/6), GSC submission, and the AI Result Tracker setup remain open and need a human.
